thread:
Stephanie Nguyen: Seeing the same objections pop up on marketplace deals (AWS esp). Can we capture these + get a 1-pager + quick talk track for Dedicated vs Private SKUs?

Top objections I’m hearing:
- “Marketplace is only for AMIs, not SaaS” / confusion on what they’re actually buying
- “Can we draw down our AWS commit?” (yes) but they want it stated plainly
- “We need VPC / Private networking, marketplace won’t work”
- “If we buy in marketplace, who supports us and what are the SLAs?”
- “How do upgrades/downgrades work? Do we get stuck?”

Would love something AEs/SEs can drop into an email + use on calls.

Markus Klein: +1. Also getting questions like “Dedicated = single tenant?” and “Private = on-prem?” People are mixing terms.

If we do a one-pager, I’d suggest:
1) 10-sec definition of Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
2) simple decision tree
3) what marketplace purchase unlocks (entitlement -> Redwood org)
4) FAQs (VPC, data isolation, audit logs, SSO, support)

Jordan Blake: Agree this is blocking late-stage procurement convos. We need consistent wording across the listing + enablement.

Two specific call-outs from last week:
- Buyers assume “Dedicated” means we deploy into *their* cloud account. We need to say it’s Redwood-managed dedicated capacity unless they want Private.
- Buyers want reassurance that marketplace doesn’t change the security posture (same platform controls) + they can still do MSA/SOW if needed.

Soojin Lee: I can draft the 1-pager + talk track as a sales enablement doc, but I need crisp bullets from PM/SE on:
- what’s included in Dedicated vs Private
- what’s configurable (regions, KMS, logging, retention)
- what’s an add-on vs included

Also any “do/don’t say” language for marketplace procurement would help (avoid overpromising around residency, etc).

Lauren Bishop: For Dedicated talk track, here’s the clean version:
- Dedicated = reserved GPU capacity in Redwood-managed env (single-customer capacity pool), predictable throughput/latency, data isolation at the service layer, faster to stand up than Private.
- Good for: enterprise performance predictability + isolation without needing to operate infra.
- Not: deployment inside customer VPC/account. If they need network-level isolation, that’s Private.

Common Q: “Is it single-tenant?” Answer: dedicated capacity and logical isolation; if they require customer-managed networking + private endpoints, go Private.

Vivek Kulkarni: For Private:
- Private = Redwood control plane + inference deployed into customer-managed VPC (and for some cases on-prem), customer controls networking, can integrate customer KMS/HSM, tighter residency/control options.
- Good for: regulated workloads, strict data perimeter requirements, “no public internet” constraints.
- Tradeoff: longer onboarding (networking setup), more coordination with their cloud/platform team.

Marketplace angle: they can procure Private via marketplace but we still do an onboarding workflow to link entitlement -> Redwood org + confirm target region/VPC details.

Markus Klein: Suggest a literal “Dedicated vs Private” table for the field:
- Where it runs
- Who manages infra
- Networking options
- Data isolation
- SLA expectations
- Typical timeline

And a 30s script:
“Dedicated is the fastest way to get predictable, isolated capacity with Redwood managing the stack. Private is for when your security posture requires the service to run inside your VPC/on-prem and you need customer-managed networking and key management.”

Laura Bennett: One procurement objection I’m hearing from finance/procurement teams: “Will the marketplace invoice be detailed enough for internal chargeback?”

We should include a line like: marketplace handles billing/invoicing; Redwood Console provides usage reporting (tokens, models, routes) for internal allocation. Also: refunds/credits follow marketplace terms (not our direct contract terms) — avoid promising custom invoicing.

Jasmine Liu: From CS side, buyers also worry they’ll be “less supported” if they buy via marketplace.

We should state:
- Support path is the same (Support portal/Slack Connect where applicable)
- SLA/support tier depends on SKU (and premium SLA add-on if purchased)
- Marketplace purchase doesn’t change incident handling/escalation

Soojin Lee: Great. I’ll draft a one-pager today and circulate for review.

Owners needed:
- @Markus Klein can you give me the SE-friendly “questions to ask” list (to route Dedicated vs Private correctly)?
- @Lauren Bishop / @Vivek Kulkarni please sanity check the table (esp. anything that could be interpreted as a guarantee)
- @Laura Bennett quick review of the procurement/invoicing wording

Target: v1 by EOD tomorrow so AEs can use it on this week’s calls.

Jordan Blake: :thumbsup: Please also include 3 common objection replies verbatim, e.g.
1) “We can’t buy SaaS through marketplace”
2) “We need everything in our VPC”
3) “Marketplace will slow us down / we can’t get support”

Make it copy/paste.

Stephanie Nguyen: +1. Also include what info to collect when they insist on marketplace:
- cloud account/org ID
- preferred region
- Redwood org email domain / admin
- which SKU + any add-ons (retention, premium SLA, compliance)

Markus Klein: Yup. I’ll send Soojin a checklist + a short call script. Also adding a “gotcha” section:
- Marketplace purchase ≠ instant production; entitlement needs linking
- If they have multiple AWS accounts, pick the purchasing account early
- Region mismatch is the #1 provisioning fail we see

Lauren Bishop: One more nuance: Dedicated can still meet a lot of “data isolation” requirements. But if they’re specifically asking for private connectivity / VPC endpoints, we should route to Private.

Vivek Kulkarni: Agree. Let’s be careful not to say Private is the only secure option. It’s the option for customer-managed network boundaries.

Soojin Lee: Got it. I’ll keep it framed as “which deployment model fits your constraints” not “security tiering.”

Stephanie Nguyen: Thanks all. Please post the draft link here when ready — I have 2 deals this week asking for exactly this.
